question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
trigger: After switching models, the user requested a fresh final-pass audit of the annotations review. Assessment and recording only; no product implementation.
requirements: Challenge all six prior semantic-unit verdicts and the strongest delete, inline, owner-move and replacement alternatives against unchanged product source.
Preserve exact model/root and mounted-view identity, transaction expiry, explicit retained-anchor ownership and one canonical native mapping authority.
Give deletion:'drop' one truthful backend-independent terminal meaning; keep exact undo recovery on nearest anchors and never revive dropped identity from equal later text.
Keep external annotation/conversation lifetime separate from document writes, inline paint and mounted-view observation.
Use one document model for a writer and a read-only reviewer while preserving independent mounted-view selection, focus, projection and read-only state.
Make borrowed annotation inputs require only the capability the index consumes; keep release/disposal with the resource owner.
Separate React-owned readers from headless lifecycle control and remove public diagnostics, recovery verbs or context machinery without a current independent caller job.
Remove active teaching for the deleted Widget carrier and document unique IDs, fault recovery and actual anchor save/restore behavior truthfully.
evidenceReuse: All six feature fingerprints and product-owner hashes from the September 20 review still match. The only changed recorded inputs were unrelated UploadClient doctrine in Plate Vision and Best API. Reused the source-bound 107/107 core and 64/64 React baseline plus the four-cohort deletion/undo probe; re-inspected AnnotationStore consumers, its fault boundary and exports, active docs, exact-view Comments adoption, mounted-view contracts and the September 3 terminal-drop decision. Two bounded adversarial source reviews independently challenged the store boundary and one-model/drop conclusions. No browser, native-device, collaboration or candidate-runtime replay was added.
summary: Pursue, superseding the prior review’s public-surface and deletion-policy ambiguity. Keep the neutral headless exact-view AnnotationStore because Plate Comments is a real cross-package consumer, but shrink the contract: borrowed annotation targets expose resolve only; React readers do not expose headless disposal or diagnostics; explicit refresh owns recovery; public metrics/status/retry and the generic provider context must earn deletion. Make drop terminal across ordinary and Authored backends, while nearest alone keeps exact undo/redo recovery. Keep the one-model/two-mounted-view consumer cut, separate decoration ownership and explicit React anchor cleanup. Active docs also teach the deleted Widget carrier and omit important input/fault/save-restore law. Six units and all six census groups reviewed, zero excluded and zero unresolved; four Pursue and two Stop.

reconciliation.question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
reconciliation.reason: Retain its lifetime split, neutral exact-view index, separate decoration owner, one-model consumer cut and React resource-owner findings. Supersede its undecided drop candidate and its decision to leave the public annotation surface untouched: prior history and current consumers support terminal drop, while source proves false release coupling, owner/reader lifecycle leakage, unearned public diagnostics and an unsafe generic provider context.

alternatives: Delete the indexing engine or inline it into Comments: reject. Plate Comments is a current cross-package consumer of exact-view resolution, node-key indexing and targeted invalidation; moving Plite view machinery into the product layer relocates the same work. Keep the truthful headless plitejs/annotations boundary.

Keep the whole current public store surface: reject. Annotation inputs are borrowed but require release; the React hook returns headless destroy/retry/diagnostic authority; getSourceStatus has no caller; metrics are test/benchmark instrumentation; retry duplicates explicit invalidation; and generic context erases TData. Preserve the engine while minimizing owner and reader capabilities.

Remove all React annotation helpers: reject as too broad. useAnnotationStore owns nontrivial commit-safe activation and cleanup for raw Plite React consumers. Keep the hook and explicit-store readers, but remove AnnotationProvider and implicit empty fallbacks unless a typed independent job is proven.

Make drop terminal across native engines: pursue. Ordinary complete-range deletion must become null and remain null through undo; Authored must not revive the dropped binding. nearest retains exact saved-history recovery. This matches the public docs, ephemeral consumers and the explicit September 3 decision.

Rename drop to a temporary fallback such as none and revive exact identity on undo: reject for this target. It conflates a plausible additional retained-identity policy with the current terminal-drop job; no current consumer requires a third policy. release remains explicit owner disposal, while drop remains target invalidation caused by deletion.

Replace two independent comment-mode documents with one model and two mounted views: pursue. Delete mirrorAnchor, JSON value replacement, selection clearing and per-comment reconstruction. Capture the anchor from the reviewer view and maintain one index per exact mounted view.

Merge persistent/scoped anchors, annotations and decorations: reject. Their lifetimes and write authority differ. Keep native mapping shared, external records outside document history and inline paint on Decoration.
Move retained-resource effects out of React state updaters and add explicit cleanup: pursue. Do not add a global resource store or factory.

Repair public teaching during adoption: pursue. Remove Widget from active navigation/guides, require unique annotation IDs, distinguish quarantined source faults from invalid input, teach explicit refresh recovery and document anchor save/restore.
proofLimits: The September 20 baseline remains source-matching: 107/107 core tests, 64/64 React tests and one public deletion/undo probe. Those passing suites encode the current backend divergence; they do not certify the target. No product code, candidate runtime, exact two-pane interaction, browser/device, collaboration or comparative scale proof was added. The surface cuts are source/consumer judgments. Design must prove terminal drop across path/point/range and save/restore, one-model mounted-view interaction and retirement, React Strict Mode cleanup, duplicate-ID failure policy and packed public exports.
